$comment: How much may happen here without a human, and the switch that stops it.
Every other control in this repository is about a CHANGE: fifteen gates, a rubric review, a
mutation drill, a revert drill, a flake drill, a post-deploy probe. All of them assume the same
unstated thing — that a maintainer reads the trail every week. That assumption is load-bearing
(~97% of commits are agent-written and Vercel ships master on push, so the weekly pass is the
only place a human sees the shape of what landed) and it was the one thing here that was never
written down, never measured, and never rehearsed. The drills cover a failing dependency and a
bad change. Nothing covered the maintainer being on holiday.
This file states the assumption so it can be acted on: who the pass belongs to, how long the
loop may run without one, which lanes run unattended and what each of them can actually WRITE,
which change classes wait for a human read no matter how green the gate is — and the pause
switch, in the one form that is reviewable, diffable and revertible: a committed flag.
$whyAFlagAndNotASetting: A repository variable or a disabled workflow is invisible in a diff, invisible in a clone, and
answers 'why is nothing running?' only to somebody who already has the settings page open. A
committed flag is read by the lane itself, shows up in `git log` with the reason attached, and
is undone by the same one-line diff that set it. It is also the shape the rest of this
repository already uses for a decision that must survive a person leaving.
$cannotSee: whether the weekly pass actually HAPPENED — nothing here observes a human reading anything, and `lastTriage` below is a claim somebody types, not a measurement;

an agent running in a local checkout: this flag is read by the lanes named under `lanes`, and a person or a harness driving Claude Code by hand is governed by AGENTS.md § What you may do unattended and by .github/agent-permissions.json, not by a JSON file;
anything already merged — pausing stops the next dispatch, it does not unwind the last one. That is `npm run revert:drill` and docs/deploy.md § Deploy + rollback;

the read-only weekly drills, which are deliberately NOT pausable (see `lanes`): they write nothing to the repository, and stopping them during an absence would remove the only evidence of what happened while nobody was looking.

pause.$howToPause: Set `paused` to true with a `reason`, a `pausedOn` date and a `pausedBy` handle, and commit it. `scripts/issue-dispatch.mjs --gate` reads this file and refuses to dispatch while it is set, printing the reason into the job summary — so a labelled issue queues instead of becoming a draft pull request. `npm run autonomy` prints the current state. Un-pausing is the same one-line diff in reverse.
pause.$whatItDoesNotStop: A push to master still deploys, the gates still run, and the weekly drills still publish their trails. This stops the lane that WRITES — the only one that can turn a sentence somebody typed into a branch and a pull request.

triage.$cadence: Monday, behind .github/workflows/agent-review-history.yml — which is what makes that workflow's trail issue the pass's agenda rather than a report nobody opens.
triage.$maxUnreadDays: Three missed passes. Not a limit anything enforces — nothing here can observe a human reading — but the number the paragraph above is worth arguing about, and the one a returning maintainer measures against: more than this, and the honest first step is `npm run review:agent -- --base <the last commit you read>` over the whole gap rather than a scroll through the log.
reads: the rubric-review trail issue (which Part A rules actually fired, and on what)
the revert + mutation drill issue (did a seeded fault survive; did a mutant)
the flake-watch issue (did the suite give two answers)
the LLM drift + candidate issue (does today's model still hold; would tomorrow's)
`npm run owners:groups` — which context groups the week's changes landed in, in triage-rank order

lanes.trigger: a maintainer applies the `agent:draft` label to an issue
lanes.writes: a branch and a DRAFT pull request; file writes are fenced to src/, test-unit/ and docs/ (ALLOWED_ROOTS in scripts/issue-dispatch.mjs) and may never touch a workflow, a gate script or an ADR
lanes.$pausable: The only lane that turns text into a change, so it is the only one where an absent maintainer changes the risk. Enforced in `gate()`, before the model is ever called.

lanes.writes: one GitHub issue, rewritten each run
lanes.$pausable: It is the triage pass's agenda. Pausing it during an absence would delete exactly the record the returning maintainer needs.

lanes.trigger: weekly (Monday 06:00 UTC), on push and on demand
lanes.writes: nothing — a job summary, an artifact and the run's own status
lanes.$pausable: Read-only, and the one lane whose finding gets WORSE with time: a dependency advisory published during an absence is the thing you most want dated.

lanes.trigger: weekly (Monday 07:00 UTC), on push and pull request
lanes.writes: nothing — it is a required check and a stage of check:ci
lanes.$pausable: Blocking. A security gate that an absence can switch off is not a gate.

lanes.trigger: weekly (Tuesday 05:00 UTC), on a change to the quick-start surface, and on demand
lanes.writes: nothing — a job summary and a 90-day artifact
lanes.$pausable: Read-only; it follows docs/open-source/self-hosting.md on a clean runner.

lanes.writes: one GitHub issue, rewritten each run
lanes.$pausable: It SPENDS money, which is the one argument for pausing it — and it is already keyed on a provider secret, so removing the key is the switch that exists, and `scripts/harness-degradation.mjs` makes the absence announce itself rather than read as a pass.

lanes.writes: one GitHub issue, rewritten each run; it seeds and restores files inside the runner's own checkout and never pushes
lanes.$pausable: Read-only with respect to this repository. It also carries the mutation drill.

lanes.writes: nothing — a job summary and an artifact

waitsForAHuman.class: arming or widening a live ad write
waitsForAHuman.why: SKLIK_WRITES_ENABLED spends an advertiser's budget. AGENTS.md § Red, rail 3 in src/lib/campaigns/mutator.ts, and two mutants in scripts/mutation-catalogue.mjs.

waitsForAHuman.class: anything that leaves the machine under the operator's name
waitsForAHuman.why: a published post, mail through Resend, a conversion uploaded to Google Ads, a person contacted. Drafts go through the review gate in `schranka`; the operator presses send.
including into a test fixture, a log line or a prompt. `.husky/pre-commit` scans and `npm run sast` blocks, and neither can see an intent.

waitsForAHuman.class: an exception list or a ratchet baseline that grows
waitsForAHuman.why: each is legitimate sometimes and each is what a lane under a wall clock reaches for. `contract:ledger:check` makes it a two-line diff; only a human decides whether the finding was fixed or absorbed (rubric B3).

waitsForAHuman.class: a change to a CODEOWNERS law file beyond what the task asked for
waitsForAHuman.why: the gates, the rubric, the ADRs and the instruction surface are what judge every other change. A lane editing them is a lane editing its own judge.
